record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: For the scent-mark-type system with a single moving species coupled to a dynamic cognitive map, namely ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇p_i g,R) and ∂_t p_i = α_ii u_i − μp_i in the one-species case, do travelling wave solutions exist when the detection function is top-hat, exponential, or Gaussian? If they do, can the wave speed be computed or estimated, how does it depend on perception and the other parameters, and can the results be extended from one species to n interacting species?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 53. Do travelling wave solutions exist solving the nonlocal system (2.11) for a single species (i.e., a single species with a dynamic cognitive map) when the detection function is chosen to be any of the forms defined in 2.3? In cases where the answer is affirmative, is it possible to compute or estimate the wave speed? How does the wave speed depend on detection function, perceptual radius, or other parameters appearing in the equation? Can these results be extended to n interacting species with cognitive map?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following nonlocal advection–reaction–diffusion system on $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{R}^d$) modelling a single species $u(x,t)\ge 0$ coupled to a dynamic cognitive map $p(x,t)\ge 0$:
$$
\partial_t u = d\,\Delta u - \gamma\,\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(u\,\nabla\,\overline{p}^{\,g,R}\bigr),\qquad
\partial_t p = \alpha\,u - \mu\,p,
$$
where $d>0$ is the diffusion rate, $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ is an advection (taxis) coefficient, $\alpha,\mu>0$ are deposition and decay rates of the cognitive map, and the nonlocal spatial averaging operator is
$$
\overline{p}^{\,g,R}(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} g_R(y-x)\,p(y,t)\,dy,
$$
with perceptual radius $R>0$ and detection function $g_R$ chosen as one of:
\begin{enumerate}
\item top-hat: $g_R(z)=\dfrac{1}{|B_R|}\mathbf{1}_{\{|z|\le R\}}$;
\item exponential: $g_R(z)=C_R\,e^{-|z|/R}$;
\item Gaussian: $g_R(z)=C_R\,e^{-|z|^2/R^2}$,
\end{enumerate}
each normalised to integrate to $1$.

(a) Do there exist travelling wave solutions $u(x,t)=U(x-ct)$, $p(x,t)=P(x-ct)$ with appropriate boundary conditions at $\pm\infty$, for each of the three choices of $g_R$?

(b) When such waves exist, can the wave speed $c$ be computed or estimated, and how does $c$ depend on the detection function $g_R$, the perceptual radius $R$, and the parameters $d,\gamma,\alpha,\mu$?

(c) Can these existence and wave-speed results be extended to the $n$-species analogue
$$
\partial_t u_i = d_i\Delta u_i - \gamma_i\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(u_i\nabla\,\overline{p_i}^{\,g,R}\bigr),\qquad
\partial_t p_i = \sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_{ij}u_j - \mu_i p_i,\quad i=1,\dots,n?
$$
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established well-posedness (existence/uniqueness of Hölder-continuous weak solutions in 1D, including the top-hat kernel) for nonlocal single-species reaction-diffusion-advection models with cognitive maps, but no published result establishes existence of travelling waves or computes wave speeds for the specified system with top-hat, exponential, or Gaussian detection functions. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Review paper listing this problem as an open question for nonlocal cognitive-map PDE models.
status_evidence.claim: The travelling-wave question for the dynamic-map single-species system is posed as an unresolved open problem.

status_evidence.title: Biological aggregations from spatial memory and nonlocal advection
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pattern formation and weak solutions for nonlocal advection-diffusion with cognitive maps; does not establish travelling waves.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses well-posedness/patterns but not travelling-wave existence or speeds.
